frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/person-months.tsx:75-91 — useBuildingUnits() calls a hand-rolled `fetch(\`/api/v1/units?buildingId=${buildingId}&limit=500\`, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } })` with NO Authorization header and NO X-Tenant-ID header. This is the ONLY raw fetch() in the entire ppt-web-core scope (routes/, lib/, hooks/, contexts/) — a repo grep confirms every other data path goes through the generated @ppt/api-client hooks or lib/api.ts's axios instance, both of which inject the bearer token (contexts/AuthContext.tsx:325-344 wires setTokenProvider + configureApiClient) and X-Tenant-ID (setOrgProvider, #1522).

ppt-web authenticates with a localStorage bearer token, not cookies: AuthContext stores ppt_access_token in localStorage and the api-client interceptor sets `bearer-token Authorization header <token>`; there is no `credentials: 'include'` cookie session anywhere. So this bare fetch reaches the authenticated GET /api/v1/units endpoint with no credentials and is rejected (401). The error is swallowed: `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(...)` -> TanStack Query catches it -> `data` is undefined -> the hook returns `units: []`.

User-facing effect (high): every person-months surface that lists units is driven by useBuildingUnits — PersonMonthsPageRoute (building summary), BulkEntryPageRoute (bulk grid), UnitPersonMonthsPageRoute (unit designation lookup). With units=[] the building summary shows ZERO units, bulk entry shows an empty grid, and unit designations render blank — the feature (Epic 3 Story 3.5) is effectively non-functional in an authenticated production session even though the page renders without an error.

Second defect on the same fetch: the response is hand-typed inline as `{ data: Array<{ id: string; unitNumber: string }> }`, bypassing the generated Unit type. If the /units envelope or field casing changes, this silently breaks with no compile-time signal — the whole reason the rest of the app uses @ppt/api-client. The query key `['person-months','building-units', ...]` also namespaces a units resource under person-months, so a units-scoped cache invalidation won't reach it.

Fix: replace the raw fetch with the generated units hook/list function from @ppt/api-client (the same module person-months already imports useBuilding/useBuildingPersonMonths from), so the request carries the bearer token + X-Tenant-ID and is typed. Confidence medium: the missing-auth-header and swallow-to-empty path are traced statically; not runtime-confirmed against a live server, but ppt-web's bearer-token contract is explicit in AuthContext.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/financial.tsx:70-86 — FinancialDashboardPageRoute runs three useQuery calls (getARAgingReport, getOverdueInvoices, listInvoices) and destructures ONLY `isLoading` from each; no `isError`/`error` is read. Line 132 passes just `isLoading={isLoading}` to <FinancialDashboardPage>; no error prop is passed and the page has no error branch.

On any of the three queries failing, the defaults kick in silently: `totals` falls back to all-zeros (lines 88-94), `invoices` to [] (95), `overdueInvoices` to [] (96). The dashboard then renders a fully 'healthy' financial picture — total balance 0, outstanding 0, overdue 0, empty invoice counts — with no indication the data failed to load. On a money-facing manager dashboard that is actively misleading (a failed AR-aging load looks identical to a genuinely clean ledger).

The correct pattern already exists a few routes down in the same file: financial.tsx:457-458 passes `error={activeQuery.error instanceof Error ? activeQuery.error.message : null}` to its page. The dashboard route should surface `isError`/`error` (aggregated across the three queries) the same way. Score 2 (unhandled error on a user-facing, financially sensitive path). New finding — distinct from the mutation onError handlers already present at lines 179/204/306/319, which cover writes, not these reads.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/OrganizationProvider.tsx:8-12 — the context value is built as a fresh object literal on every render (`const value = user?.organizationId ? { organizationId, organizationName } : null`) and passed straight to <OrganizationContext.Provider value={value}>. Because a new reference is produced each render, every consumer of OrganizationContext re-renders whenever OrganizationProvider re-renders, even when organizationId/organizationName are unchanged.

OrganizationProvider sits high in the tree (fed by useAuth()), so it re-renders on any AuthContext value change (isLoading toggles, token refresh re-deriving user, etc.), fanning unnecessary re-renders to all org-context consumers. Fix: wrap `value` in useMemo keyed on [user?.organizationId, user?.organizationName] — matching the useMemo pattern AuthContext itself uses for its own context value (AuthContext.tsx:591). Low severity (perf/refactor smell), but a clean, landable, zero-risk fix.

Fix: add .timeout(...)/.connect_timeout(...) (or reuse a single pooled client stored on AppState) for the three SSO reqwest clients

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/listings/page.tsx:112-124 — getFiltersFromUrl parses five range params directly with bare Number(): `if (priceMin) filters.priceMin = Number(priceMin)` (L112), priceMax (L115), areaMin (L118), areaMax (L121), roomsMin (L124). searchParams values are attacker/user-controllable via the URL; `/en/listings?priceMin=abc` yields filters.priceMin = NaN with no Number.isFinite guard.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/listings/page.tsx:144 — `const currentPage = Number(searchParams.get('page') || 1)`. `?page=abc` -> NaN; `?page=0` -> 0; `?page=-5` -> -5; `?page=1.5` -> 1.5. No clamp to a positive integer.

frontend/packages/reality-api-client/src/listings/hooks.ts:22-44 (buildQueryString) — NaN is not undefined, so `if (filters.priceMin !== undefined) params.set('priceMin', String(filters.priceMin))` (L31) emits the literal string `priceMin=NaN`; likewise `params.set('page', String(page))` (L23) emits `page=NaN`. Full traced path: URL -> getFiltersFromUrl -> useListings(filters, currentPage) (page.tsx:145) -> buildQueryString -> `fetch(${getApiBase()}/api/v1/listings?...&priceMin=NaN&page=NaN)` (hooks.ts:51-53). The malformed query string is certain; the backend's 400/degrade response is the only unconfirmed part (static analysis).

The correct guard already exists in the same app: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/realtor/ListingForm.tsx:54-63 (parseOptionalNonNegative) trims, rejects `!Number.isFinite(num)` and `num < 0`, and price validation at L97-98 uses `!Number.isFinite(priceNum) || priceNum <= 0`. The public search parser simply doesn't apply the same discipline.

Fix: in getFiltersFromUrl, coerce each range param through a helper that drops the key when `!Number.isFinite(n)` (and optionally when negative); clamp currentPage to `Math.max(1, Math.trunc(n))` with a NaN fallback of 1. Keeps a stale/hand-edited/bookmarked URL from firing a malformed request.
